newsitem.title: USA: Chubb earnings boosted by personal insurance lines.
newsitem.headline: Chubb earnings boosted by personal insurance lines.

text.p: Chubb Corp. on Tuesday reported higher second-quarter profits, helped by strong underwriting, especially in its personal lines business.
Operating income in the quarter rose to $175.6 million, or $1.01 per share, in line with analysts' consensus estimate as compiled by First Call.
In the year-ago quarter, the Warren, N.J.-based insurer had operating income of $156.8 million or 89 cents per share.
Net income in the latest quarter rose to $188.7 million, or $1.09 a share, from $174.3 million, or 98 cents a share.
The increased earnings came amid a more than 3 percent drop in the average number of shares outstanding as the company continued to buy back stock.
"We continue to produce strong results despite exceedingly poor market conditions," Chubb Chief Executive Dean O'Hare said in a statement.
"This quarter again demonstrates the kind of consistent earnings growth our organisation can produce, absent significant catastrophes, even in the face of prolonged pricing weakness," O'Hare said.
Net property and casualty premiums written in the second quarter increased 8.8 percent to $1.4 billion, and the combined ratio fell to 95.3 percent, compared with 96.3 percent last year.
The combined ratio is a key measure of underwriting profitability. An underwriting profit occurs when the combined ratio falls below 100 percent.
"Overall, underwriting was very, very good and it was helped by outstanding results in certain lines and sectors," said Dillon Read analyst Michael Lewis.
Underwriting results were particularly strong in the personal lines business, where the combined ratio fell to 84.4 percent from 87.5 percent in the year-ago quarter.
Chubb's real estate business recorded losses after taxes of $6.4 million for the quarter, compared with income of $3.0 million a year ago.

This reflects the terms of an agreement reached in June to sell a substantial portion of Chubb's commercial real estate properties to a joint venture formed by Paine Webber Real Estate Securities Inc. and Morgan Stanley Real Estate Fund II LP.
Chubb said it repurchased about 2.2 million shares of its common stock in the open market in the second quarter, bringing the total purchases in 1997 to nearly 8.0 million shares.

In the second quarter, Chubb Capital Corp. called for redemption of the remaining outstanding exchangeable subordinated notes. Prior to the redemption, note-holders elected to convert the notes into common stock, resulting in the issuance of nearly 5 million shares.
